text: Every storm on Earth...
on one planet.
Hurricanes.
Auroras.
Blizzards.
And a super storm.
Watch till the end. The super storm hits at eight fifty, and you do not want to miss it.
This is our planet, seen from deep space.
Over the next ten minutes, we're going to fly through every kind of sky it has.
Welcome to Pro Weather.
Here's the plan for today's journey.
Seven chapters. Twelve cities. A hurricane, auroras, a storm at sea, a blizzard... and at the very end, the super storm.
Let's go!
Chapter one. Twelve cities, ranked from coldest to hottest, using our sample data.
Number twelve: Reykjavik, at minus four degrees. Freezing!
Number eleven: Moscow, minus two.
Number ten: London, nine degrees. Grab a jacket.
Number nine: Paris, eleven degrees.
Number eight: New York, twelve.
Number seven: Tokyo, eighteen degrees. Perfect weather.
Number six: Cape Town, twenty one.
Number five: Sydney, twenty four.
Number four: Cairo, twenty seven. Now it's getting hot. But who is number one?
Number three: Rio de Janeiro, twenty nine.
Number two: Delhi, thirty one degrees.
And number one... Mumbai! Thirty three degrees. The hottest city on our list.
Chapter two. We're flying inside a hurricane.
From up here, you can see the giant spiral arms, turning around one calm center.
A category five hurricane has winds of two hundred and fifty two kilometres per hour, or more.
Now, we start to descend.
Down through the clouds... closer, and closer.
Some hurricanes are more than one thousand kilometres wide.
And now, we drop straight into the eye.
Welcome to the eye of the storm. Look around. It can be calm in here, even sunny, while a wall of wind spins all around us.
Time to climb back out.
Next up... lights in the polar sky.
Chapter three. The aurora.
We're above the North Pole, on the dark side of the planet.
Auroras glow more than one hundred kilometres above the ground.
Those green and purple curtains are moving, dancing, changing every second.
They happen when the solar wind from the Sun meets our atmosphere.
Honestly, it's one of the most beautiful things in nature.
Don't leave now. The halfway point is next.
Halfway there! And trust me... the best part is still coming.
Coming up: a thunderstorm at sea.
A blizzard in the mountains.
And then... the super storm.
Chapter four. A thunderstorm, in the middle of the ocean.
Listen to that rain. The waves are rising, and the lightning is getting closer.
Did you know? Lightning is about five times hotter than the surface of the Sun.
There are no buildings here. No shelter. Just the storm, and the sea.
Around the world, lightning strikes about forty four times every second.
Now we rise above the waves, to see the storm from the sky.
Next up... we get lost in a blizzard.
Chapter five. The blizzard.
Snow, wind, and almost zero visibility. We're flying through a frozen mountain valley.
To be called a blizzard, winds must reach fifty six kilometres per hour, with visibility under four hundred metres.
Stay low... follow the valley...
And those conditions have to last for three hours or more.
Now let's climb. Up, above the storm...
and look at those peaks!
Next up: twenty four hours, in sixty seconds.
Chapter six. Day and night.
Watch the sun race across the sky.
Look closely. As night falls, the city lights switch on.
Every sunrise, every sunset, happening in just seconds.
Here, one full day passes in about sixteen seconds.
But something is changing. The clouds are getting darker.
Next up... the moment you've been waiting for.
Chapter seven. The super storm.
Three.
Two.
One.
Every storm. All at once.
A giant hurricane is forming, lightning is hitting everywhere, and the whole planet is going dark.
This is the biggest storm we have ever simulated.
Hold on...
And then... the storm passes.
The sun comes back. The planet breathes again.
So... which city should we fly into next? Tell us in the comments.
And subscribe, so you don't miss part two.
Part two. Storms of the future. Coming soon.
